subject: Post-call: Ledgerly model-pathways & parity sprint proposal
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.d@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@ledgerly.com>; Bryan Cho <bcho@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: recommended models, acceptance thresholds, next steps

Thanks again for taking the call today — good conversation and helpful product context. Short recap and concrete next steps so we can align on a parity sprint.

Summary (what we heard)
- Primary Ledgerly flows: invoice extraction including line-item splitting, vendor normalization, and duplicate detection.
- Hard constraints: <50 ms median token latency for synchronous QA paths; data residency in US; auditability for sampled logs.
- Quality bar: accuracy on entity extraction (vendor/name/date/amount) and dedup F1 are the top KPIs.

Our recommended model pathways (to evaluate in a 2-week sprint)
1) Open-model candidate (cost-forward): Mistral-1.3B-instruct / Llama-3-13B-quant (4-bit) — expect good instruction-following; will require prompt engineering and targeted prompt sets.
2) High-capacity open (cost+quality): Llama-3-70B-ptq for heavier cases (batching).
3) Proprietary baseline: LedgerlyBase-v2 (your current internal baseline) — we'll run head-to-head on the same prompt set and slice.

Acceptance thresholds (proposed for parity decision)
- Entity extraction F1 >= 0.92 on the labeled 2k sample (micro-average).
- Dedup detection AUC >= 0.95 and F1 >= 0.88 at operating threshold.
- No quality regressions on the top-50 high-value customers (manual review sample).

Instrumentation & evaluation plan
- We'll run closed evaluation on a de-identified 2k sample you supply. Metrics we’ll capture: token-level latency distribution, per-class precision/recall, confusion matrices, and answer provenance.
- We'll provide the prompt set we used (attached) and the benchmark CSV with initial runs.
- If open models meet thresholds, we'll test a small canary in your staging environment under Redwood Dedicated.

Ask / next steps
1) Please confirm you can deliver a de-identified 2k labeled slice by EOD Thu Jan 20 (we need the data to start runs).
2) Sign off on the proposed acceptance thresholds or send edits (reply inline).
3) Confirm security/residency constraints — if you need an on-prem evaluation package we can escalate with Product.

Attachments: ledgerly_eval_promptset_v1.zip (prompt templates + rubric), openmodel-bench-20270118.csv (initial smoke runs)

I'll kick off the benchmark queue as soon as we have the sample. If you'd like, we can set a 30-minute sprint kickoff for Fri Jan 21.

Cheers,

Priyom Das

Looping in a couple of evaluation details from the MLP side. Quoting Elena: 
> "Can you include one example prompt that you plan to use for vendor normalization? Also, what's your suggested negative-sampling strategy for dedup detection?"

Vendor normalization prompt (example)
--
System: You are a normalization assistant. Extract vendor names and return the canonical vendor name using Ledgerly's vendor taxonomy. Do not hallucinate — if uncertain, return "UNKNOWN" and provide confidence.
User: Input: "Acme, Inc."
Assistant: {"canonical_name": "Acme, Inc.", "confidence": 0.98}
--

Negative-sampling for dedup detection
- Construct near-duplicates by swapping date formats, abbreviating company types (Co. vs Company), and introducing OCR-like noise (character swaps).
- Include hard negatives from true duplicates with slight differences in amounts to ensure model does not overfit on amount match alone.

Evaluation notes
- We'll compute per-field F1 and then a weighted aggregate per invoice (weights: vendor 0.35, amount 0.25, date 0.15, line-items 0.25).
- For dedup, in addition to AUC/F1 we'll provide per-threshold precision/recall curves so Ledgerly can pick an operating point that matches business tolerance.

Operational: Ben will queue the initial smoke runs on Thursday (using the included promptset); we can iterate prompts quickly after first-pass outputs.
